sections.h2: Where is Cedar Falls, Iowa, and how is the city laid out?
sections.html:
Cedar Falls is a city in Black Hawk County, Iowa, in the Waterloo-Cedar Falls metropolitan area, where Waterloo is the other principal city. Its ZIP code is 50613 and its area code is 319.

The city covers roughly 30 square miles at an elevation of 879 feet. Hartman Reserve Nature Center sits inside the city limits and holds forest, prairie and wetland. For a seller, the practical point is that Cedar Falls is a separate municipality with its own services, even though many buyers and employers treat it as one market with Waterloo next door.

The Census Bureau estimates 41,240 residents as of July 1, 2025. The 2020 census counted 40,713, which ranked the city 13th in Iowa.

sections.h2: How did Cedar Falls grow into the city it is now?
sections.html:
Cedar Falls began in March 1845 when William R. Sturgis and Erasmus D. Adams started a settlement called Sturgis Falls, renamed Cedar Falls around 1850. Water power drove the early economy, with a sawmill built by the Overman family in 1848 and a gristmill in 1850.

The city was the first county seat of Black Hawk County in 1853, but an April 1855 referendum moved the seat to Waterloo. Cedar Falls was incorporated as a city in 1865. The Illinois Central Railroad arrived in 1861, and by 1893 four railroad lines served the town.

The biggest later change came after the Iowa State Normal School opened on September 6, 1876. It grew into the University of Northern Iowa. Population climbed from 14,334 in 1950 to 36,322 in 1980, so the city grew to about 2.5 times its 1950 size in three decades.

sections.h2: What shapes the Cedar Falls economy?
sections.html:
The University of Northern Iowa is the city's major institution, and the older industrial base still shows in the record. Milling, foundries, woodworking and machinery all played a part, and Viking Pump, an industrial pump maker, was founded in Cedar Falls in 1911. Sartori Hospital was established in 1915.

Retail followed the postwar growth: College Square Mall opened in 1969. The 2020 median age of 31.4 is young for Iowa, a figure that fits a city built around a university.

The metro area spans two cities, so Cedar Falls and Waterloo share a labor market. A seller who is relocating within it should check which city's rules and school district apply to the next address.

sections.h2: Which school districts serve a Cedar Falls house?
sections.html:
Cedar Falls Community Schools serves most of the city. The district includes Cedar Falls High School, two junior high schools and seven elementary schools.

A small section of the city falls in the Waterloo Community School District, so the district for a given address should be checked before it is described in a listing or a sale conversation. Private options include Valley Lutheran High School and a Catholic elementary school at St. Patrick Catholic Church.

The Malcolm Price Lab School, also known as Northern University High School, closed in 2012 after cuts at UNI. Older neighbors may still mention it, but it no longer operates.

sections.h2: What utilities come with a Cedar Falls home?
sections.html:
Cedar Falls owns its own power, gas, water and cable TV services, operated as Cedar Falls Utilities.

  • Call the utility early to schedule final meter readings for the closing date.
  • Ask for any unpaid balance in writing, since it should be settled before the sale is final.
  • Mention the internet service in the home: the utility began offering gigabit speeds on January 14, 2015, and PC Magazine named it the nation's fastest internet in 2020.

The Metropolitan Transit Authority of Black Hawk County runs public bus service, which matters to owners of houses near campus or the library at 524 Main Street.

sections.h2: What does Iowa require when a Cedar Falls house is sold?
sections.html:
Iowa adds a few filings to a sale that Cedar Falls owners should plan for. Each one is set by statute and handled through the county recorder.

  • Real estate transfer tax: under Iowa Code 428A.1 the tax is 80 cents for each $500 of value, or fraction of $500, and it does not apply when there is no consideration. The statute does not say which side pays, so the purchase agreement decides.
  • Declaration of value: this form goes to the recorder with the deed. Iowa Code 428A.2 lists the transfers that are excused from it.
  • Groundwater hazard statement: under Iowa Code 558.69, the seller reports wells, burial sites, underground tanks, hazardous waste, solid waste disposal sites and private sewage systems on the property.

The recorder must refuse a deed that is missing a required statement. Recorders cannot charge a fee for filing the groundwater statement.

sections.h2: When do Black Hawk County property taxes become delinquent?
sections.html:
Iowa property tax is paid in two installments, and each one turns delinquent on a fixed day. The first installment is delinquent from October 1 and the second from April 1, according to Iowa Code 445.37.

If September 30 or March 31 lands on a weekend, delinquency moves to the second business day of the next month. A payment mailed with correct postage must be postmarked before the delinquent date to avoid interest.

When a Cedar Falls house sells in the middle of a tax year, the buyer and seller normally split the bill by the closing date. The county treasurer can confirm what has been paid so the closing figures match.

sections.h2: What problems do Cedar Falls sellers usually run into?
sections.html:
Most delays come from paperwork about the property itself, plus whatever work an older house needs. The city has been growing since the 1840s, and the population jumped sharply between 1950 and 1980, so houses of very different ages and conditions sit side by side.

  • A private well, septic system or buried tank that has to be disclosed on the groundwater hazard statement.
  • A house with deferred repairs that makes a traditional buyer's inspection list long.
  • A tenant in place or a lease that ends at a bad time.
  • An inherited home where the title is not yet in the heirs' names.

Each of these can slow a conventional sale. Selling to a cash buyer removes the loan appraisal step, though the recorder filings above still apply.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale of a Cedar Falls house work?
sections.html:
A cash sale in Cedar Falls follows the same recording steps as any other sale, with fewer moving parts before closing. You describe the house, the buyer reviews it, and an offer is made on the house as it stands.

  1. Share the address and condition of the house.
  2. Review the written offer and ask any question about it.
  3. If you accept, a title company or attorney prepares the deed, the declaration of value and the groundwater hazard statement.
  4. Sign, record at the Black Hawk County Recorder, and receive the proceeds.

You can decline an offer and owe nothing. Compare it with the cost and time of listing before you decide.

faqs.q: How many people live in Cedar Falls, Iowa?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimates 41,240 residents as of July 1, 2025. The 2020 census counted 40,713, which ranked Cedar Falls 13th among Iowa cities.

faqs.q: Is Cedar Falls in Black Hawk County?
faqs.a: Yes. Cedar Falls is in Black Hawk County and is part of the Waterloo-Cedar Falls metropolitan area. It was the first county seat in 1853, before an April 1855 referendum moved the seat to Waterloo.

faqs.q: What transfer tax applies when I sell a house in Cedar Falls?
faqs.a: Iowa charges 80 cents for each $500 of value, or fraction of $500, under Iowa Code 428A.1. No tax applies when there is no consideration. For a hypothetical $200,000 value, that works out to $320, and the contract sets who pays it.

faqs.q: Do I have to disclose a well or septic system when selling in Cedar Falls?
faqs.a: Yes, if the property has one. Iowa Code 558.69 requires a groundwater hazard statement that reports wells, private sewage systems, underground tanks, burial sites and certain waste conditions. If none exist, the deed carries a short statement saying so.

faqs.q: When is the second property tax installment delinquent in Iowa?
faqs.a: It becomes delinquent on April 1. If March 31 falls on a weekend, delinquency starts on the second business day of April.
